title: Variational problem with a submanifold of endpoint pairs
notes: The action is \(I(\gamma)=\int_0^T f(\gamma,\dot\gamma)\,dt\), with \((\gamma(0),\gamma(T))\in R\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\). Fixed endpoints and the diagonal \(R\) are examples.
statement: Let \(R\) be smooth and \(f\) be \(C^2\) near a smooth critical path. Allowed variations satisfy \((v(0),v(T))\in T_{(\gamma(0),\gamma(T))}R\). Stationarity consists of the Euler--Lagrange equation and \((-p(0),p(T))\in N^*R\), where \(p=f_{\dot\gamma}\).
reconstruction: The momentum condition and regularity assumptions are additions. An arbitrary smooth Lagrangian need not define a \(C^2\) action on all of \(H^1\); the Hessian along the smooth path is used here.
fate: The setup appears in \citet[\S1]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: this is standard regular variational calculus.

title: Positive Legendre condition gives a finite Morse index
notes: Positivity of \(f_{\dot\gamma\dot\gamma}\) is said to make the number of negative squares finite.
statement: On a compact time interval, suppose \(A(t)=f_{\dot\gamma\dot\gamma}(\gamma(t),\dot\gamma(t))\) is continuous and positive definite. The second variation on the closed \(H^1\) space of admissible endpoint variations, including the boundary term from \(R\), has finite negative index.
reconstruction: Compactness makes the Legendre bound uniform. Lower-order terms and endpoint traces are compact relative to the positive derivative form after adding an \(L^2\) term.
fate: See \citet[\S1]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the assertion is valid under these hypotheses.

title: Legendre transform and the symplectic variational flow
notes: Euler--Lagrange equations become Hamilton equations; \(\Phi(t)\) is the derivative of the flow along the extremal.
statement: An invertible velocity Hessian gives the local Legendre transform \(p=f_v(q,v)\), \(H(q,p)=p\cdot v-f(q,v)\). In a symplectic trivialization along the extremal, the linearized flow satisfies \(\Phi(0)=1\) and \(\Phi(t)^*\sigma=\sigma\).
reconstruction: Only local invertibility is needed.
fate: See \citet[\S1]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the Hamiltonian reduction is established.

title: Graphs of symplectic maps as Lagrangian planes
notes: The page writes \(\varphi(t)=\operatorname{graph}\varphi(t)\) and says that \(\sigma\oplus(-\sigma)\) vanishes on the graph.
statement: For symplectic \(V\) of dimension \(2n\), \(\Lambda(t)=\{(v,\Phi(t)v):v\in V\}\) is Lagrangian in \((V\oplus V,\sigma\oplus(-\sigma))\) exactly when \(\Phi(t)\) is symplectic.
reconstruction: Upper-case \(\Phi\) is the map and \(\Lambda\) the subspace.
fate: See \citet[\S\S1--3]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the equivalence is elementary and exact.

title: Symmetric-form chart on the Lagrangian Grassmannian
notes: For \(\alpha\cap\beta=0\) and \(\gamma\cap\beta=0\), write \(\gamma=\operatorname{graph}\Gamma\), \(\Gamma:\alpha\to\beta\), and \(Q(u,v)=\sigma(\Gamma u,v)\).
statement: Relative to \(V=\alpha\oplus\beta\), every plane transverse to \(\beta\) is such a graph. It is Lagrangian exactly when \(Q\) is symmetric, and \(\gamma\cap\alpha=\ker Q\) under the graph identification.
reconstruction: The phrase that \(\sigma\) vanishes on \(\Gamma\) means on its graph.
fate: See \citet[\S2]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the coordinate description is standard.

title: Maslov crossings and independence of the auxiliary complement
notes: At a simple crossing \(\gamma(t)\cap\alpha\ne0\), take the jump of the quadratic-form index; it does not depend on the transverse \(\beta\).
statement: For a Lagrangian path with endpoints transverse to \(\alpha\), signed regular crossings of \(\Sigma_\alpha=\{\Lambda:\Lambda\cap\alpha\ne0\}\) define an integer. Symmetric-form charts give compatible local counts; homotopies with fixed transverse endpoints preserve the integer.
reconstruction: Perturbation defines nonregular crossings. A symplectic sign convention fixes the sign.
fate: See \citet[\S2]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the Maslov index is established; endpoint conventions remain essential.

title: Topology of the Lagrangian Grassmannian and the singular Maslov cycle
notes: The notes call \(\Sigma_\alpha\) an embedded two-sided hypersurface and infer \(\pi_1(\operatorname{Lag})=\mathbb Z\); its complement is identified with quadratic forms.
statement: For \(N\geq1\), \(\operatorname{Lag}(\mathbb R^{2N})=U(N)/O(N)\) has fundamental group \(\mathbb Z\). Transverse planes form a contractible symmetric-matrix chart. The one-dimensional-intersection stratum is a cooriented smooth hypersurface; higher-intersection strata are singular when \(N\geq2\).
reconstruction: The whole cycle is not smooth. The complement description alone is not a proof of the fundamental group.
fate: Compare \citet[\S2]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the topological conclusion is correct, but the literal smoothness assertion is not.

title: Endpoint correction for an open Lagrangian path
notes: The proposed index is \([\gamma:\alpha]+\operatorname{ind}Q\{\gamma(T),\alpha,\gamma(0)\}\); in dimension one it is described by completing an arc on a circle.
statement: An open-path Maslov index needs an endpoint normalization. For triples admitting the graph chart, a triple quadratic form measures the change of reference plane. The Hörmander identity supplies a reference-independent correction. Degenerate endpoints require a specified extension.
reconstruction: The notes define neither all nontransverse triple forms nor an unambiguous orientation of the circle completion.
fate: Compare \citet[\S2, formula (2.4)]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the construction is known, but some notebook conventions are undetermined.

title: The conormal Lagrangian for a boundary condition
notes: The notes define \(R^\perp\) with reversal of the second momentum, write \(\rho=T(R^\perp)\), and call it a fibre of the normal bundle.
statement: Under \((x,y;\xi,\eta)\mapsto(x,\xi;y,-\eta)\), \(N^*R\) is Lagrangian in the doubled phase space. Its tangent at the endpoint covector is the required Lagrangian \(2n\)-plane \(\rho\).
reconstruction: This is a tangent to the total conormal bundle; a fibre has dimension \(2n-\dim R\).
fate: See \citet[\S1]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the geometry is correct after the tangent/fibre distinction.

title: General-boundary Morse--Maslov index formula
notes: The equality is \(\operatorname{ind}_R\gamma=\operatorname{ind}(\varphi)+i(I,\rho,\varphi(T))+\dim\pi(\rho\cap I)-2n\), with \(i=(\operatorname{ind}+\operatorname{null})Q\).
statement: Under regularity and the positive Legendre condition, the Morse index is computable from flow graphs, the boundary conormal Lagrangian, and endpoint forms. The fixed-endpoint specialization is \(\operatorname{ind}\gamma=\sum_{0<t<T}\dim\{J:J\text{ is Jacobi},\,J(0)=J(t)=0\}\), with endpoint nullity separate.
reconstruction: The general equality is retained as an announcement. Its absolute constant and triple-index convention cannot be recovered from the transverse-chart definition: \(\varphi(0)=I\), and \(\rho\cap I\) may be nonzero. The precise fixed-endpoint specialization is an editorial reconstruction.
fate: See \citet[\S3, formulas (3.1)--(3.4)]{duistermaat1974morse}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the general theorem is established; the exact notebook normalization is partially matched.

title: Spherical convolution and kernels on a compact quotient
notes: For \(X=K\backslash G/\Gamma\), the kernel is \(K_\varphi(x,y)=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\varphi(x\gamma y^{-1})\), with bi-\(K\)-invariant \(\varphi\).
statement: Let \(G\) be connected semisimple with finite centre, \(K\) maximal compact, and \(\Gamma\) torsion-free cocompact. For \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(K\backslash G/K)\), the locally finite kernel is smooth on \(X\times X\), hence trace class. Invariant differential operators arise from suitable distributions supported at the identity coset.
reconstruction: Torsion-freeness makes \(X\) a manifold. In the bi-\(K\)-invariant realization on \(G\), identity-coset support means support on \(K\).
fate: The setup is reviewed in \citet[\S\S2--3]{duistermaatkolkvaradarajan1979spectra}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the compact-quotient construction is established.

title: Commuting spherical operators and a common eigenbasis
notes: The spherical convolution algebra is commutative with involution; its compact operators have common orthonormal eigenvectors \(e_j\).
statement: For the Riemannian symmetric pair \((G,K)\), bi-\(K\)-invariant convolution is commutative. On compact \(X\), spherical smoothing operators and an invariant elliptic Laplacian have a complete orthonormal simultaneous eigenbasis. Eigenvalue functionals are multiplicative characters.
reconstruction: An elliptic operator or approximate identity supplies completeness; compactness alone would leave a possible common kernel.
fate: See \citet[\S3]{duistermaatkolkvaradarajan1979spectra}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the joint decomposition is standard.

title: Trace formula and the grouping into conjugacy classes
notes: The notes equate \(\sum_j\lambda_j(\varphi)\), the diagonal integral, and a sum of individual \(\int_X\varphi(x\gamma x^{-1})\,dx\).
statement: The trace is the diagonal integral. Its geometric expansion is a sum over \(\Gamma\)-conjugacy classes with centralizer-volume factors and orbital integrals. An individual \(\varphi(x\gamma x^{-1})\) generally does not descend to \(X\); an ungrouped sum can be integrated over a specified fundamental domain.
reconstruction: Class regrouping repairs the quotient-invariance gap. One can instead integrate over a specified fundamental domain, but the notes do not say so.
fate: The normalized side is in \citet[Theorem 5.1]{duistermaatkolkvaradarajan1979spectra}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the trace identity is established with this interpretation.

title: Abel transform and the Euclidean spherical transform
notes: The map is \(f(a)=e^{\langle\rho,a\rangle}\int_N\varphi(an)\,dn\); the margin calls \(A\) a vector space.
statement: Use \(G=KAN\), write \(a=\exp H\), and put \(\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha>0}m_\alpha\alpha\). With compatible Haar measures, \(\mathcal A\varphi(H)=e^{\rho(H)}\int_N\varphi(\exp H\,n)\,dn\) identifies spherical convolution with convolution on \(C_c^\infty(\mathfrak a)^W\).
reconstruction: Restricted-root multiplicities and exponential coordinates are additions.
fate: See \citet[\S\S2--3]{duistermaatkolkvaradarajan1979spectra}.
present_status: As of November 2026: this is classical, with measure-dependent normalization.

title: Joint spectral parameters and multiplicities
notes: Multiplicativity gives \(\lambda_j(\varphi)=\widetilde f(\mu_j)\), with \(\mu_j\in A_\mathbb C^*\); these form the spectrum.
statement: A spherical eigencharacter is evaluation at a parameter in \(\mathfrak a_\mathbb C^*/W\). Joint eigenspaces are counted with dimension. Representatives before the Weyl quotient are noncanonical, and nonprincipal parameters need not lie on the real spectral axis.
reconstruction: Multiplicities and the Weyl quotient are needed for the counting formula.
fate: See \citet[\S3]{duistermaatkolkvaradarajan1979spectra}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the parametrization is established.

title: Poisson form of the spherical trace identity
notes: The trace becomes \(\sum_j\widetilde f(\mu_j)=\sum_\gamma\langle T_\gamma,f\rangle\), for a locally finite family.
statement: For compact \(X\), the joint spectral distribution is a sum of \(W\)-invariant distributions indexed by conjugacy classes, with centralizer-volume weights. Nonidentity terms avoid a common neighbourhood of zero. The identity term is quotient volume times the Fourier transform of spherical Plancherel measure, with fixed Haar normalization.
reconstruction: Weights and normalization are supplied from the paper.
fate: See \citet[Theorem 5.1]{duistermaatkolkvaradarajan1979spectra}, received July 1978 and published 1979.
present_status: As of November 2026: the distributional formula is proved.

title: Closed-geodesic length and support of the geometric distribution
notes: The boxed assertion reads \(\ell(\gamma)=\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{supp}T_\gamma,0)\).
statement: For nontrivial \(c\), the matched theorem places \(\operatorname{supp}T_c\) in a Weyl union of affine subspaces at distance equal to the minimal translation length \(\ell(c)\). For real regular Iwasawa classes, including rank one, \(T_c\) is a nonzero sum of Dirac masses on that Weyl orbit, giving equality of distances.
reconstruction: A general support inclusion gives a lower bound, not itself equality. Equality is verified here in the explicit regular case.
fate: See \citet[Theorems 5.1--5.2 and Proposition 5.15]{duistermaatkolkvaradarajan1979spectra}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the regular case is established; the universal equality is partially verified.

title: Joint Weyl law and the unsupported remainder exponent
notes: The last line gives a ball count with main term \(\operatorname{vol}(X)\int_{\operatorname{ball}(R)}\beta\) and \(O(R^{n-r-1})\); the middle exponent letter is uncertain.
statement: For bounded open principal spectral \(\Omega\) with smooth boundary, the matched result is \(\sum_{\lambda\in R\Omega}m(\lambda)=c_G\operatorname{vol}(X)\int_{R\Omega}\beta+O(R^{n-1})\), \(n=\dim X\). Complementary parameters are separately controlled; rank one gives \(O(R^{n-1}/\log R)\).
reconstruction: These are verified conclusions, not a claim that the extra exponent symbol is absent from the scan.
fate: See \citet[Theorems 8.8--8.9 and 9.1]{duistermaatkolkvaradarajan1979spectra}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the classical bounds are established; the stronger exponent was not verified.

title: Matrix differential-operator algebra and three compatibility equations
notes: The coefficients are \(\mathcal B=M_\ell(\mathcal B_0)\), where \(\mathcal B_0\) consists of meromorphic germs in \(x\), \(x,t\), or \(x,t,y\). The targets are \([L,P]=0\), \(L_t=[P,L]\), and a displayed Zakharov--Shabat equation.
statement: Form the Ore algebra \(\mathcal B[\partial_x]\) with \(\partial_x b=b\partial_x+\partial_x(b)\). The stationary equation is commutation; the Lax equation is compatibility of \(L\psi=\lambda\psi\) and \(\psi_t=P\psi\). Two evolution equations \(\psi_y=L\psi\), \(\psi_t=P\psi\) have compatibility \(L_t-P_y=[P,L]\).
reconstruction: Commutators mean \([A,B]=AB-BA\). The sign correction is justified again in the dedicated zero-curvature item.
fate: The framework is summarized in \citet[Ch.~III, \S2]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: these operator equations are standard.

title: Filtered bimodule data and the omitted generation axioms
notes: The notes specify a \((\mathcal B,\mathcal O)\)-bimodule \(M\), a filtration, a distinguished \(\mathbf1\), and \(\nabla(bm)=b_xm+b\nabla m\), referring backwards for further axioms.
statement: A sufficient precise version is an exhaustive filtration \(M_0=0\subset M_1\subset\cdots\), \(M_1=\mathcal B\mathbf1\), with each quotient free of rank one, and \(\nabla M_i\subset M_{i+1}\) inducing isomorphisms on consecutive quotients. The right action of the commutative algebra \(\mathcal O\) commutes with \(\nabla\) and the left \(\mathcal B\)-action, and is faithful.
reconstruction: These are the generation and commutation hypotheses needed below, supplied from the referenced earlier axioms and the matched exposition. The notebook alone does not repeat them.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~III, \S2.2]{manin1978algebraic}, Russian original 1978, English 1979.
present_status: As of November 2026: the reconstruction data are established.

title: A free cyclic differential module produces commuting operators
notes: The lemma makes \(M\) a free rank-one \(\mathcal B[\partial_x]\)-module, with \(\partial_x\) acting as \(\nabla\); \(\mathbf1\varphi=L_\varphi\mathbf1\).
statement: Under the preceding filtration axioms, \(\mathbf1,\nabla\mathbf1,\ldots,\nabla^{i-1}\mathbf1\) are a \(\mathcal B\)-basis of \(M_i\). Thus evaluation at \(\mathbf1\) identifies \(\mathcal B[\partial_x]\) with \(M\). Each right multiplication by \(\varphi\in\mathcal O\) determines \(L_\varphi\), and \(\varphi\mapsto L_\varphi\) is an injective algebra map; its image is commutative.
reconstruction: Faithfulness gives injectivity. This does not say that arbitrary operators commuting with one chosen \(L\) automatically form this algebra. The scalar specialization \(\ell=1\) is the filtered-module reconstruction mechanism in GP-1975-26; the occurrence does not replace its pointed-curve and local-data hypotheses by a bare curve and bundle. Matrix coefficients and the later explicit nodal examples are additional scope, not a changed definition of that earlier problem.
fate: The precise reconstruction is \citet[Ch.~III, Theorem 2.4]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the cyclic-module theorem is proved.

title: A commuting time connection yields a Lax equation
notes:
The notes add \(
abla_t\), require \([
abla_x,
abla_t]=0\), and obtain \(L_t=[P,L]\).
statement:
Let \(
abla_t\) extend \(\partial_t\), commute with \(
abla_x\), and commute with the right \(\mathcal O\)-action. Define \(P\) by \(
abla_t\mathbf1=P\mathbf1\). Then \(\partial_tL_\varphi=[P,L_\varphi]\).
reconstruction: Compatibility with the spectral-ring action is needed in addition to the displayed commutator.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~III, Theorem 2.5]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated construction is established.

title: Zero curvature and the sign in the Zakharov--Shabat equation
notes: The page has \(L_t+P_y=[P,L]\), while \(\nabla_t\mathbf1=P\mathbf1\), \(\nabla_y\mathbf1=L\mathbf1\), and the three connections commute.
statement: With the displayed connection convention and \([A,B]=AB-BA\), the resulting identity is \(L_t-P_y=[P,L]\). Indeed \([\nabla_t-P,\nabla_y-L]\mathbf1=(-L_t+P_y+[P,L])\mathbf1=0\); cyclic freeness makes the operator vanish.
reconstruction: This is a mathematical emendation, not a claim that the scan has a minus. Independent visual inspection of the published English Theorem~2.6, p.~83, confirms a printed plus rather than an OCR artifact. Its connection conventions likewise require a difference; the notebook and publication both need a mathematical sign correction.
fate: Compare \citet[Ch.~III, Theorem 2.6 and its proof]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: zero curvature is established with the corrected sign.

title: An affine nodal spectral curve by pairwise identification
notes: The ring is \(\mathcal O=\{f\in k[\lambda]:f(\alpha_i)=f(\beta_i),\,1\leq i\leq N\}\).
statement: For \(2N\) pairwise distinct complex numbers \(\alpha_i,\beta_i\), this subring is the coordinate ring of the affine line with the \(N\) pairs identified as ordinary nodes. Its normalization is \(\mathbb A^1\). For a real model the node set and identifications must be invariant under conjugation.
reconstruction: Pairwise distinctness of all \(2N\) points is stronger than the notebook's explicitly written \(\alpha_i\ne\alpha_j\), and excludes unintended multiple identifications.
fate: The exact construction is \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.1]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: this spectral-curve construction is established.

title: Gluing a trivial module over the normalization
notes: Inside \(N=\mathcal B[\lambda]^r\), the module is defined by \(m(\alpha_i)=g_i m(\beta_i)\); the left \(\mathcal B\)-action is componentwise right multiplication by \(b^t\).
statement: Write the ambient module as \(\mathcal N=\mathcal B[\lambda]^r\) to distinguish it from the number of nodes. The left action \(b\cdot(m_j)=(m_jb^t)\) commutes with left block matrices \(g_i\in GL_r(\mathcal B_\mathbb C)\). The gluing equations define a left \(\mathcal B\), right \(\mathcal O\) sub-bimodule, the algebraic analogue of sections of a bundle with prescribed nodal gluing.
reconstruction: The transpose is essential for associativity of this left action; it is not a transcription error.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~III, \S\S5.1--5.2]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the module model is established.

title: Reality conditions at conjugate nodes
notes: For real \(k\), the notes put \(\alpha_i=\overline{\beta_i}\) and \(\overline{g_i}=g_i^{-1}\).
statement: Work first over the complexification of the real coefficient algebra. At conjugate paired nodes, conjugating \(m(\alpha_i)=g_i m(\beta_i)\) gives the same condition precisely when \(\overline{g_i}g_i=1\). Taking the fixed real subspace then descends the module.
reconstruction: The points cannot all be required to lie in \(\mathbb R\) as well as to be distinct conjugate pairs. The scalar field in the initial point list must be complexified.
fate: These conditions appear in \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.1]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the real descent condition is valid with complexified node parameters.

title: The staircase filtration on polynomial columns
notes: In \(N_{ar+k}\), the first \(k\) components have degree at most \(a\), the remaining components degree at most \(a-1\), \(0\leq k<r\).
statement: For \(a\geq0\), define \(\mathcal N_{ar+k}\) by those bounds, interpreting degree at most \(-1\) as zero. Then \(\mathcal N_0=0\), the filtration is exhaustive, and each successive quotient is a free left \(\mathcal B\)-module of rank one.
reconstruction: The boundary convention \(a=0\) is explicit; it matters for the later shift.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.3]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the filtration is established.

title: The block interpolation matrix and nondegeneracy
notes: The block matrix has entries \(\alpha_i^j I_r-\beta_i^jg_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,N\), \(j=0,\ldots,N-1\); the notebook requires nonzero determinant.
statement: Assume \(G=(\alpha_i^jI_r-\beta_i^jg_i)_{i,j}\) is invertible in \(M_{rN}(\mathcal B)\). If \(M_{(i)}=M\cap\mathcal N_i\), then \(M_{(rN)}=0\), and \(M_{(i)}/M_{(i-1)}\to\mathcal N_i/\mathcal N_{i-1}\) is an isomorphism for \(i>rN\).
reconstruction: Over a matrix coefficient algebra the clean condition is invertibility. A scalar determinant is taken only after expanding into matrices over the commutative coefficient ring and restricting to a locus where it is a unit.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.4 and Lemma 5.5]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the interpolation lemma is proved.

title: The sign and indexing of the filtration shift
notes: After \(M_{(rN)}=0\), the definition reads \(M_i=M_{(i-rN)}\), but the generator is then placed in \(M_1\).
statement: With the notebook's one-based convention \(M_0=0\), \(M_1\) generated by \(\mathbf1\), the correct shift is \(M_i=M_{(i+rN)}\). With the paper's generator in \(M_0\), it is \(M_i=M_{(i+rN+1)}\).
reconstruction: The negative shift leaves the supposed first generator space zero and is incompatible with the preceding vanishing lemma. The one-unit difference between conventions must not be mistaken for another error.
fate: Compare \citet[Ch.~III, Lemma 5.5]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the corrected positive shift is definite.

title: Normalized cyclic vector from finite linear equations
notes: The normalized vector is \(\mathbf1=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}m_j\lambda^j+\lambda^Ne_1\), with a displayed system using \(m_i\) inside the sum over \(j\).
statement: Its coefficients uniquely solve \(\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(\alpha_i^jI_r-\beta_i^jg_i)m_j=-(\alpha_i^NI_r-\beta_i^Ng_i)e_1\), \(1\leq i\leq N\), under invertibility of \(G\).
reconstruction: The summation coefficient must be \(m_j\), not the row-indexed \(m_i\).
fate: The normalized vector is \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.6, equation (5)]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the finite linear construction is established.

title: Connection preserving the nodal gluing equations
notes: For \(\nabla_x=\partial_x+d_x(\lambda)\), the notes give \(\partial_xg_i=g_id_x(\beta_i)-d_x(\alpha_i)g_i\).
statement: Let \(d_x\in M_r(\mathcal B[\lambda])\), acting on columns on the left. The displayed differential equations imply \(\nabla_xM\subset M\); differentiating the gluing relation proves this directly. Such matrices are \(\mathcal B[\lambda]\)-linear endomorphisms of the ambient module under the transpose action.
reconstruction: The notebook's equality with all \(\mathcal B\)-linear endomorphisms is too broad: commuting with multiplication by \(\lambda\) is additionally required.
fate: This is \citet[Ch.~III, Lemma 5.8]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the preservation criterion is established.

title: Explicit evolution of the gluing matrices
notes: For constant \(d_x(\lambda)\), \(g_i(x)=e^{-xd_x(\alpha_i)}g_i(0)e^{xd_x(\beta_i)}\).
statement: If \(d_x\) is independent of \(x\), the displayed formula solves the gluing-preservation equation for every invertible initial \(g_i(0)\). Matrix exponentials are required even when \(r=1\) if the coefficient algebra has matrix size \(\ell>1\).
reconstruction: The marginal assertion that \(r=1\) gives ordinary scalar exponentials additionally requires \(\ell=1\), or scalar commuting coefficients.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.9]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the explicit evolution is established.

title: Flatness of the parameter connections and two-time exponential signs
notes: The notes write \(\partial_xd_t-\partial_td_x=[d_x,d_t]\), and later put \(+td_t(\alpha_i)\) in the left exponential as well as \(+td_t(\beta_i)\) on the right.
statement: For \(\nabla_x=\partial_x+d_x\), \(\nabla_t=\partial_t+d_t\), flatness is \(\partial_xd_t-\partial_td_x+[d_x,d_t]=0\). For constant commuting matrices the compatible solution is \[g_i(x,t)=e^{-xd_x(\alpha_i)-td_t(\alpha_i)}g_i(0,0)e^{xd_x(\beta_i)+td_t(\beta_i)}.\]
reconstruction: Both signs follow by differentiation. Choosing \(d_t,d_y\) as scalar polynomials in \(d_x\) ensures commutation; arbitrary constants need not commute.
fate: Compare \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.12, equations (9)--(10)]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the equations hold with these corrected signs.

title: Graded cyclicity and the order of a spectral operator
notes: The lemma \(\operatorname{ord}L_\varphi=r\deg\varphi\) ends with an unfinished condition. A matrix pattern and the example \(\begin{pmatrix}0&\lambda\\b&0\end{pmatrix}\) follow.
statement: Assume \(\nabla_x\) increases filtration by one and is invertible on successive graded pieces. Multiplication by a polynomial \(\varphi\in\mathcal O\) of degree \(d\) raises the staircase filtration by exactly \(rd\), giving \(\operatorname{ord}L_\varphi=rd\). For \(r=2\), the displayed matrix has the required graded property when \(b\) is invertible.
reconstruction: The unfinished hypothesis is supplied from the adjacent graded-isomorphism condition, not guessed solely from the desired order. For general \(r\), a cyclic lower subdiagonal with invertible entries and an invertible \(\lambda\)-coefficient in the upper-right corner suffices.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~III, Lemma 5.10 and \S\S5.11--5.13]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the conditional order formula is proved.

title: A quadratic function on the nodal curve and an operator of order twice the rank
notes: If \(\alpha_i+\beta_i\) is independent of \(i\), there is \(\psi\in\mathcal O\) of degree two, hence an operator of order \(2r\).
statement: If every pair is distinct and \(\alpha_i+\beta_i=s\), then \(\psi(\lambda)=\lambda^2-s\lambda\) has equal values at paired points. Under the graded-cyclicity hypotheses, \(L_\psi\) has order \(2r\), including order four for \(r=2\). Conversely, a genuine quadratic polynomial constant on all pairs forces their sums to agree.
reconstruction: The explicit polynomial and converse follow by factoring \(\psi(\alpha)-\psi(\beta)\).
fate: The degree/order application appears in \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.13 and \S6]{manin1978algebraic}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the construction is established.

title: The rank-one nodal construction includes KdV multisolitons
notes: The notes identify the rank-one case with \(N\)-soliton solutions of KdV and its hierarchy.
statement: Take scalar coefficients \(\ell=1\), spectral rank \(r=1\), paired spectral points with a common sum, and the nodal gluing data of the preceding construction. On any parameter domain where the interpolation determinant is nonzero, the quadratic spectral function gives a second-order scalar differential operator. Choosing the compatible cubic time flow yields the KdV Lax equation after the usual normalization; its nodal specialization includes the classical multisoliton family.
reconstruction: This does not assert that every arbitrary gluing matrix yields a globally smooth real soliton. The real multisoliton subclass needs real spectral choices and a nonvanishing real denominator; the notebook states neither global regularity nor those restrictions.
fate: The identification is explicit in \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.13]{manin1978algebraic}. The rank-one multisoliton family is treated there as known, whereas the uniform higher-rank module construction is the newer part.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated local construction includes the established rank-one soliton family.

title: The unqualified question about N-soliton behaviour
notes: The talk ends with \ru{Вопрос: поведение \(N\)-солит. решения?}.
statement: No equation, spectral rank, reality or nonsingularity conditions, time direction, or requested observable is specified in the final question.
reconstruction: It cannot be equated with the earlier two-soliton phase-shift problem GP-1973-54 or promoted to a new higher-rank scattering conjecture merely because of the preceding examples.
fate: The surrounding soliton construction is matched by \citet[Ch.~III, \S5.13 and \S6]{manin1978algebraic}, but no definite final question was identified.
present_status: As of November 2026: the final question is too underspecified to support an open-problem claim.

title: The programme of an elementary geometry of polyhedra
notes: Gelfand says that an elementary geometry of higher-dimensional polyhedra remains to be made; he contrasts commutative planar rotations with noncommutative \(SO(3)\).
statement: The contrast concerns the search for local combinatorial characteristic-class formulas. Noncommutativity of \(SO(3)\) is a definite fact, but the assertion that three-dimensional polyhedra have no substantive theory specifies no mathematical obstruction or question.
reconstruction: No universal nonexistence statement or orphan problem is extracted from this programme. The claim that named mathematicians learned from the GGL work is recorded as Gelfand's recollection, not independently established intellectual genealogy.
fate: The contemporary programme is described in \citet[introduction, p.~105]{macpherson1978combinatorial}; it is not an exact theorem matching the rhetoric.
present_status: As of November 2026: the programme is identifiable, but no definite open proposition is stated.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The two-faces condition does not characterize a manifold
notes: Every \((n-1)\)-simplex is said to bound exactly two \(n\)-simplices.
statement: For a finite pure simplicial complex, this is the codimension-one incidence condition of a pseudomanifold without boundary. To obtain a PL manifold one must also impose the appropriate sphere links at every simplex; incidence alone is insufficient.
reconstruction: The notebook's use of this condition as a description of the intended polyhedral manifold needs the link condition. MacPherson additionally formulates his flattenability hypotheses.
fate: Compare \citet[introduction, pp.~105--106]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the distinction between pseudomanifolds and PL manifolds is standard.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Assigning local vertex weights for the Euler characteristic
notes: Gelfand asks how numbers at vertices can sum to the Euler characteristic and invokes angular defects.
statement:
For a finite simplicial complex \(K\), the vertex weights
 \[w(v)=\sum_{\sigma\ni v}\frac{(-1)^{\dim\sigma}}{\dim\sigma+1}\]
 satisfy \(\sum_vw(v)=\chi(K)\). For a closed piecewise Euclidean triangulated surface, the angle defects
 \[\kappa(v)=2\pi-\sum_{\sigma\ni v}\theta_{\sigma,v}\]
 satisfy \(\sum_v\kappa(v)=2\pi\chi(K)\).
reconstruction: These are precise reconstructions of the local-counting question. The notebook's external-angle sentence does not identify which angles it sums and should not be read as the displayed \(2\pi\) formula without explanation.
fate: The classical Euler formula is recalled in \citet[introduction, p.~105]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the definite local Euler-characteristic question has elementary established answers.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Two degree-four characteristic numbers
notes: Gelfand says that four-dimensional polyhedra have two invariants, the Euler characteristic and one more.
statement: For a closed oriented smooth four-manifold, the characteristic numbers in view are \(\langle e(TX),[X]\rangle=\chi(X)\) and \(\langle p_1(TX),[X]\rangle=3\,\operatorname{sign}(X)\). These do not classify four-manifolds and are not their only topological invariants.
reconstruction: The statement is interpreted within the local characteristic-class programme, not as a classification claim.
fate: The Euler/Pontryagin context is explicit in \citet[introduction, p.~105]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the characteristic-number interpretation is established.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The first Pontryagin cycle as a corank-two degeneracy locus
notes: Four generic vector fields on a four-manifold give \(Z=\{x:\operatorname{rk}(e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4)\leq2\}\), a codimension-four signed set.
statement: Let \(E\) be a real rank-four bundle on a smooth closed oriented four-manifold. A generic bundle map \(\mathbb R^4\to E\) meets the rank-two stratum transversely and avoids lower ranks. The resulting zero-cycle, with the standard determinantal coorientation, represents the Poincaré dual of \(p_1(E)\). Apply this to \(E=TX\).
reconstruction: Genericity means transversality to rank strata; the rank-at-most-one locus has codimension nine and is avoided. The sign convention is normalized by \(p_1\) of an oriented plane bundle being its Euler class squared.
fate: The degeneracy-cycle framework underlies \citet[\S1]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975computation}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the construction is classical and was expository here.

title: Canonical coorientation and independence of the signed count
notes: The rank degeneracy set in \(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb R^m,\mathbb R^n)\) is said to carry a canonical coorientation; the signed count does not depend on the chosen fields.
statement: For a square map of corank two, the normal space to the rank stratum is \(\operatorname{Hom}(\ker A,\operatorname{coker}A)\), with both factors two-dimensional. Its determinant transforms by even powers, so a fixed universal orientation convention is independent of bases. A generic homotopy of sections gives a compact oriented cobordism of the zero-cycles.
reconstruction: The assertion is restricted to the corank-two square situation actually used; arbitrary determinantal strata need not have a canonical coorientation.
fate: See the section-change framework of \citet[\S1]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975computation}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the signed homology class is independent of the generic fields.

title: Two sections of a plane bundle represent the square of the Euler class
notes: For a two-dimensional real bundle \(E\), \(Z=\{e_1=e_2=0\}\) is identified with its first Pontryagin cycle.
statement: For an oriented real rank-two bundle over a closed oriented four-manifold, a transverse section \((e_1,e_2)\) of \(E\oplus E\) has zero-cycle dual to \(e(E\oplus E)=e(E)^2=p_1(E)\).
reconstruction: Orientation is supplied so that the ordinary integral Euler class notation is unambiguous. The canonical orientation of \(E\oplus E\) also admits a formulation without orienting \(E\), but that extension is not needed here.
fate: This is the plane-bundle model used in \citet[\S1]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975computation}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the model is established.

title: A one-chain relating cycles after replacing one section
notes: The first identity is \(Z(e_2,e_3)-Z(e_1,e_3)=\partial Z^1(e_1,e_2;e_3)\), with \(e_3=0\), \(e_1=\lambda e_2\), \(\lambda>0\).
statement: For generic sections of a real plane bundle, use the compactified parameter \(\lambda\in[0,\infty]\). The incidence locus \(e_3=0,\ e_1=\lambda e_2\), projected as an oriented chain to the base, has boundary the difference of the two zero-cycles, with sign fixed by the parameter orientation.
reconstruction: The chain is the closure or pushforward of the parameterized locus; the open set with \(\lambda>0\) alone has no included boundary points. Transversality and compactification are explicit additions.
fate: The section-change calculus is developed in \citet{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975calculus}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the cobordism identity is established after orientation conventions.

title: A two-chain filling the cyclic sum of section changes
notes: Adding three displayed one-chain boundaries gives a closed curve; it is said to bound the locus \(e_1=\lambda e_2=\mu e_3\), \(\lambda,\mu>0\).
statement: For generic triples, compactify the positive proportionality parameters and take the corresponding oriented incidence chain. Its codimension-two projection has boundary equal to the cyclic sum of the three codimension-three section-change chains, with compatible signs.
reconstruction: The parameter compactification and signs are necessary for a chain identity; the notebook gives the geometric idea rather than a complete orientation convention.
fate: This is part of the published hypersimplicial chain calculus \citep{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975calculus}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the geometric chain relation is established.

title: Hypersimplices and their two kinds of triangular faces
notes: A hypersimplex is the convex hull of centres of faces of a simplex. Vertices carry index sets; the octahedron has triangular faces of two types.
statement: The standard hypersimplex is \(\Delta(k,m)=\{x\in[0,1]^m:\sum_i x_i=k\}\), the convex hull of indicator vectors of \(k\)-subsets. Scaling by \(1/k\) identifies these with barycentres of \((k-1)\)-faces. Its faces are obtained by fixing coordinates to zero or one; \(\Delta(2,4)\) is an octahedron whose triangular faces arise in the two ways.
reconstruction: The notebook's appended fixed indices correspond to coordinates fixed to one.
fate: See \citet[\S1, pp.~107--109]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the combinatorial definition is standard.

title: Boundary-compatible chains assigned to hypersimplices
notes: The task is to construct a chain for each hypersimplex with the required properties; vertices represent double-zero loci and edges represent the one-section changes.
statement: Construct rational chains \(C(H)\) in spaces of vector configurations, extending the specified vertex and edge assignments, so that \(\partial C(H)=C(\partial H)\), with the appropriate codimension and compatibility under restriction to faces. In the first-Pontryagin construction these chains must descend through the configuration and hypersimplicial complexes.
reconstruction: The boundary equation is the strongest definite compatibility indicated by the preceding examples. The full list of admissibility and locality properties is supplied by the published construction, not repeated by the notebook.
fate: The chain systems already exist in \citet[\S18, Proposition 14; \S\S27--28]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975calculus}; compare \citet[\S3]{macpherson1978combinatorial}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the first-Pontryagin chain problem was solved before this talk; no new unsolved variant is specified.

title: The two triangular chain assignments and the handwritten one-half
notes: One triangle with labels \(14,24,34\) points to \(\tfrac12(e_4=0)\); the other, labelled \(12,13,23\), points to positive proportionality of \(e_1,e_2,e_3\).
statement: These drawings distinguish the two triangular face types. The second has the incidence interpretation in the preceding two-chain item. The first shows a rational coefficient \(1/2\), but the notes do not specify the oriented region, multiplicity function, or chain category needed to interpret \(\tfrac12\{e_4=0\}\) as a complete boundary-compatible chain.
reconstruction: The PNG confirms the coefficient. It is not corrected to an integer and is not promoted to a fully defined chain formula.
fate: The surrounding rational chain construction is identifiable in \citet[\S3]{macpherson1978combinatorial}, but the isolated drawn assignment is only partially specified.
present_status: As of November 2026: the diagram belongs to a known construction; its literal chain convention remains undetermined.

title: The affine complex line transform
notes: A line is \(x_1=\alpha_1x_3+\beta_1,\ x_2=\alpha_2x_3+\beta_2\), and \(\varphi(\alpha,\beta)\) is the integral of \(f\) against \(dx_3\,d\bar x_3\).
statement: For \(f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb C^3)\), define \(\varphi(\alpha,\beta)=\int_{\mathbb C}f(\alpha_1t+\beta_1,\alpha_2t+\beta_2,t)\,dA(t)\). This chart excludes directions parallel to \(x_3=0\); changing the line parameter transforms the density by the corresponding squared Jacobian.
reconstruction: The area-measure convention and chart limitation are explicit additions. A global scalar realization uses the compensating density factor of the cited paper.
fate: See \citet[\S1, equations (1)--(4)]{gelfand1967planes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the line transform is classical.

title: Reconstruction from all line integrals and reduction to a plane
notes: The notes ask how to recover \(f\) from \(\varphi\), call the data redundant, and restrict to lines in a plane.
statement: For a fixed complex two-plane through \(x\), the supplied line integrals over its lines are the complex Radon transform of \(f\) restricted to that plane. Its inversion recovers \(f(x)\); taking all such planes gives uniqueness of the full line transform on Schwartz functions.
reconstruction: The restriction is to lines contained in the chosen plane, not a projection of \(f\) onto that plane.
fate: The precise cycle inversion is \citet[\S8, Theorem 2]{gelfand1967planes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the reconstruction problem is solved.

title: John equation and the missing global range hypotheses
notes: In the real case \(\varphi_{\alpha_1\beta_2}=\varphi_{\alpha_2\beta_1}\), and the equation is said to be sufficient.
statement: For the real line transform in \(\mathbb R^3\), differentiation under the integral gives this equation. It characterizes the range within the global smooth line-data class whose density-normalized derivatives decay faster than every inverse power of the line's distance from zero, uniformly in compact direction charts, with the correct coordinate covariance.
reconstruction: A local smooth solution in one affine chart, with no decay or global extension, is not covered by sufficiency. The condition \(k<n-1\) in the paper holds for \(k=1,n=3\).
fate: See \citet[\S7, Theorem 1 and its real-case footnote]{gelfand1967planes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the range theorem is established in its stated global class.

title: A wavefront-set heuristic from singular plane integrals
notes: The page suggests that \((x_0,\xi_0)\in WF(u)\) when integration over parallel planes in direction \(\xi_0\) has a singularity.
statement: For a localized distribution, Radon data can detect conormal singularities through the incidence canonical relation. An unlocalized integral over a whole plane does not identify which point caused a singularity, and cancellations can erase contributions. Thus a pointwise criterion requires localization near \(x_0\), a convention making \(\xi_0\) a normal covector, and a precise microlocal implication.
reconstruction: These are necessary qualifications, not a theorem present in the notebook. No unique equivalence is reconstructed from the single sentence.
fate: The related characteristic geometry is explained in \citet[\S\S2--3]{guillemin1985line}; the notebook's particular wavefront criterion is not matched.
present_status: As of November 2026: the heuristic is recognizable, but its literal pointwise assertion is insufficiently specified.

title: Differential forms on the space of lines through a point
notes: In the complex case \(\mathcal H\varphi=\sum_{i,j}\varphi_{\beta_i\bar\beta_j}\,d\alpha_i\wedge d\bar\alpha_j\); in the real case \(\mathcal H\varphi=\sum_i\varphi_{\beta_i}\,d\alpha_i\). Substitute \(\beta_i=x_i-\alpha_i x_3\).
statement: The substitution pulls the relevant differentiated data back to the pencil of lines through \(x\). In the indicated chart it gives a complex \((1,1)\)-form, or a real one-form. With the line-density transformation law these expressions patch to forms on the projective space of directions.
reconstruction: Global patching and measure normalization are implicit in the handwritten chart formula.
fate: See \citet[\S\S4--6]{gelfand1967planes}; differential-form generalization in \citet[\S1]{gelfand1969forms}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the differential-form construction is established.

title: The closed-form characterization of the complex line-transform range
notes: The theorem is \(\varphi=Rf\Longleftrightarrow d(\mathcal H_x\varphi)=0\) for every \(x\).
statement: Let \(\varphi\) be globally smooth normalized line data in the rapidly decreasing class: all derivatives in local vector-bundle trivializations of the affine Grassmannian decay rapidly in the transverse displacement, uniformly over directions. Then \(\varphi=Rf\) for some \(f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb C^3)\) exactly when the associated \((1,1)\)-form is closed on the pencil through every \(x\).
reconstruction: The global class is essential and is not contained in the notebook's displayed equivalence.
fate: This is \citet[\S7, Theorem 1]{gelfand1967planes}, published ten years before the seminar.
present_status: As of November 2026: the characterization is proved.

title: Cycle inversion and the real dimension of the integrating cycle
notes: The inversion formula is \(\int_\gamma\mathcal H_x\varphi=c_\gamma f(x)\); the cycle is called one-dimensional.
statement: For data in the range and a closed real two-cycle \(\gamma\) in the complex projective direction space \(\mathbb{CP}^2\), the formula holds with a constant depending only on its homology class and density normalization. A projective line is a cycle with nonzero coefficient and gives reconstruction.
reconstruction: A \((1,1)\)-form has real degree two. The notebook's dimension is interpretable as complex dimension one, not real dimension one. A nontrivial cycle also cannot be contained entirely in the contractible affine direction chart.
fate: See \citet[\S8, Theorem 2, pp.~29--30 of the Russian original]{gelfand1967planes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: cycle inversion is established with the corrected dimension convention.

title: Why the analogous real local period gives zero
notes: For the real case the notes say \(C_\gamma=0\), and inversion is nonlocal.
statement: For real Schwartz line data in the range, the closed real one-form on the pencil has zero periods: \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathbb{RP}^2)=0\). This particular local differential-form period cannot reconstruct \(f(x)\); a real inversion uses a different, nonlocal operator.
reconstruction: The conclusion is about this period formula, not a claim that the real line transform lacks an inverse.
fate: The distinction follows from the real range form and complex inversion theorem in \citet[\S\S7--8]{gelfand1967planes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the obstruction to this particular local period is established.

title: Restricted data and the definition of an admissible complex
notes: For a three-dimensional family \(K\) of lines, the notes ask when knowing \(\mathcal H\varphi\) on \(K\) permits recovery of \(\varphi\).
statement: In the matched 1968 formulation, \(K\) is a closed irreducible algebraic three-dimensional family of complex lines covering a dense open subset of \(\mathbb C^3\). Admissibility means the inversion form on \(K\cap G_x\) can be computed by a differential operator from restricted scalar data \(\varphi|_K\), independently of an extension off \(K\). Reconstruction additionally requires a cycle with nonzero inversion coefficient.
reconstruction: The notebook's question supplies differentiated data, whereas the published definition asks whether those derivatives descend from scalar restricted data. These distinct inverse problems must not be identified without this correction.
fate: See \citet[\S2, Definitions 1--2 and formula (7)]{gelfandgraev1968complexes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the classical admissibility problem is formulated and solved in that setting.

title: Admissible line complexes come from a curve or a surface
notes: The asserted alternatives are all lines meeting a curve or all lines tangent to a surface.
statement: For the algebraic admissibility notion just stated, a complex of lines in \(\mathbb C^3\), near a generic regular line and its regular critical point, is either the family meeting a local curve or the family tangent to a local surface. The general-dimensional theorem imposes distinct critical points and general-position tangent hyperplanes; the paper states the three-dimensional dichotomy as its corollary.
reconstruction: This is not a classification of arbitrary smooth three-parameter families with any conceivable injectivity property. Singular global branches and the data model require the paper's hypotheses.
fate: See \citet[\S5, Theorem 6 and corollary, pp.~49--51]{gelfandgraev1968complexes}; compare \citet[\S3]{guillemin1985line}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the identified classification predates the talk.

title: Plücker coordinates and the equation of a linear complex
notes: For a plane spanned by \(x,y\in k^4\), \(p_{ij}=x_i y_j-x_j y_i\); a linear complex satisfies \(\sum c_{ij}p_{ij}=0\).
statement: A projective line in \(\mathbb P^3_k\), \(k=\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\), is a two-plane in \(k^4\). Its decomposable bivector \(x\wedge y\) gives a point of the Klein quadric in \(\mathbb P(\Lambda^2k^4)\). A linear complex is its hyperplane section, equivalently the two-planes isotropic for an alternating form \(\omega\).
reconstruction: The plane in the notebook is the vector two-plane representing a projective line.
fate: The Grassmannian framework is recalled in \citet[\S\S1--2]{guillemin1985line}; this is classical projective geometry.
present_status: As of November 2026: the construction is established.

title: Symplectic polarity attached to a nondegenerate linear complex
notes: Each point is associated with a plane containing the complex's lines through it; each line is associated with another line meeting those lines.
statement: If \(\omega\) is nondegenerate, the plane of complex lines through \(p=[v]\) is \(\mathbb P(v^\perp)\). A line \(\mathbb P(L)\) has polar line \(\mathbb P(L^\perp)\). Every isotropic line meeting \(\mathbb P(L)\) also meets \(\mathbb P(L^\perp)\).
reconstruction: Nondegeneracy is needed for a polarity. If \(v\in\ker\omega\), all lines through \(p\) satisfy the complex equation, and no single projective plane contains them.
fate: This is the alternating-form realization of the classical line geometry underlying \citet[\S2]{guillemin1985line}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated polarity is valid in the nondegenerate case.

title: The standard linear complex and its isomorphism class
notes: The example is \(x_1=\alpha x_3+\beta,\ x_2=\gamma x_3+\alpha\); the notes say any other complex is isomorphic to it.
statement: In homogeneous coordinates this is the affine chart of \(p_{14}+p_{23}=0\), a rank-four alternating form. All nondegenerate alternating forms on \(k^4\) are linearly equivalent. Rank-two forms give a different projective orbit: their complexes consist of lines meeting the projectivized kernel.
reconstruction: The universal assertion must be restricted to nondegenerate linear complexes. It does not classify all nonlinear complexes and does not prove admissibility for restricted scalar line data.
fate: The linear-algebra normal form supplies the correction; compare the admissibility distinction in \citet[\S2]{gelfandgraev1968complexes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the nondegenerate normal form is established; the unqualified assertion is false.

title: An unspecified Legendre transformation
notes: The single line says \ru{Преобр. Лежандра есть}.
statement: No source space, target space, generating function, or transformation formula is given. Contact or projective duality associated with the line complex is a possible interpretation, but is not uniquely determined.
reconstruction: No specific Legendre transform is inserted into the notebook.
fate: The phrase was compared with the cited integral-geometry papers and the line-complex literature; no exact transformation was identified.
present_status: As of November 2026: the intended transformation remains unidentifiable from this record.

title: When does the Poncelet polygon close?
notes: A polygon is inscribed in one conic and tangent to another; Gelfand asks when such a polygon closes, citing Griffiths.
statement: For two nonsingular complex plane conics whose incidence curve of a point on the outer conic and a tangent to the inner conic is smooth, that curve is genus one. The successive-tangent operation is translation by a fixed \(\delta\) on it. A polygon closes after \(m\) steps exactly when \(m\delta=0\); exact period \(m\) requires \(\delta\) to have exact order \(m\). Nested real ovals select the real branch and direction of iteration.
reconstruction: Smoothness of the incidence curve excludes degenerate conic pairs. The elliptic-curve translation is the precise reconstruction behind the notes' mention of Jacobi's elliptic integrals.
fate: See \citet[\S I(d), pp.~345--348]{griffiths1976abel}, published before the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: the closure criterion is classical and solved.

title: Poncelet’s porism
notes: If the construction closes from one point, it closes from every other point in the same number of steps.
statement: For the nondegenerate conic pair and consistent tangent iteration above, the existence of a closed \(m\)-step orbit means the elliptic translation is \(m\)-torsion. Therefore its \(m\)th iterate is the identity for every admissible starting point. Exceptional points of the algebraic construction are understood by extension.
reconstruction: The same branch and a nondegenerate conic pair are required; changing tangent directions arbitrarily is not this map.
fate: The porism is stated in \citet[\S I(d), formula (1.37) and discussion]{griffiths1976abel}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the theorem is classical.

title: Invariant measure and circle-rotation coordinates
notes: The notebook writes that the Poncelet theorem implies an invariant measure and an isomorphism with a circle rotation.
statement: For nested smooth real conics with a regular real Poncelet map, the elliptic-curve parameter gives an invariant positive measure on the relevant circle component. Integrating and normalizing this measure gives a coordinate conjugating the map to a rigid rotation. Rational rotation number is the closure criterion.
reconstruction: The construction uses the elliptic geometry and a full-support nonatomic invariant density. The mere logical statement of a porism does not supply such a density or the conjugacy.
fate: The elliptic-parameter construction is in \citet[\S I(d)]{griffiths1976abel}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the geometric rotation description is established, with the stated regularity.

title: Figiel’s short proof of Dvoretzky’s theorem
notes: Gelfand points to the latest Compositio issue and attributes the simplest proof of Dvoretzky's theorem to Figiel.
statement: For every integer \(k\geq2\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), there is \(N(k,\varepsilon)\) such that every real or complex normed space of dimension at least \(N(k,\varepsilon)\) has a \(k\)-dimensional subspace with Banach--Mazur distance at most \(1+\varepsilon\) from the corresponding Euclidean space.
reconstruction: This is a bibliographically identifiable pointer; the notebook contains no details of the proof and makes no quantitative claim about \(N\).
fate: The exact source is \citet[theorem, p.~297]{figiel1976short}, Compositio 33(3), 1976.
present_status: As of November 2026: the theorem and the cited proof predate the talk.

title: Symmetric groups, partitions, and Young diagrams
notes: The notes define \(S_n\), finitary \(S_\infty\), and a descending array of left-aligned rows called a Young tableau.
statement: \(S_\infty=\bigcup_nS_n\) under the inclusions fixing the last letter. A partition \(\lambda_1\geq\lambda_2\geq\cdots\geq0\), \(\sum\lambda_i=n\), specifies a Young diagram. A standard tableau additionally labels its cells \(1,\ldots,n\), increasingly in rows and columns.
reconstruction: The distinction between an unfilled diagram and a labelled tableau is editorial terminology; the notebook uses the Russian word for tableau for both.
fate: This is the classical framework recalled in \citet[\S\S1,5]{vershikokounkov2005approach}; the asymptotic setting is explicit in \citet[p.~1024]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}.
present_status: As of November 2026: these definitions are standard.

title: The common constituent of row and column induced representations
notes: For the row subgroup \(G_1\) and column subgroup \(G_2\), the notes induce the trivial and alternating representations and select their one common irreducible constituent.
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(R_\lambda\) and \(C_\lambda\) permute the labelled cells within each row and column. The representations \(\operatorname{Ind}_{R_\lambda}^{S_n}{\bf1}\) and \(\operatorname{Ind}_{C_\lambda}^{S_n}\operatorname{sgn}\) have just one common irreducible constituent, \(V^\lambda\), with multiplicity one in both. The resulting \(V^\lambda\) exhaust the irreducible representations.
reconstruction: The field and multiplicity are made explicit. A different labelling gives conjugate subgroups and the same representation class.
fate: The traditional Young construction is recalled in \citet[Introduction]{vershikokounkov2005approach}; the paper's new inductive proof is later, but the theorem itself is classical.
present_status: As of November 2026: this is established characteristic-zero representation theory.

title: Hook-length formula for the degree of an irreducible
notes: The page gives \(n!/\prod h\) and dates the hook formula to 1955; its hook description mentions the cells to the right and below.
statement: For \(\lambda\vdash n\), \(d_\lambda=\dim V^\lambda=n!/\prod_{(i,j)\in\lambda}h_{ij}\), where \(h_{ij}=\lambda_i-j+\lambda'_j-i+1\). The corner cell itself is included.
reconstruction: The \(+1\) is essential. Interpreting the notebook's verbal description as excluding the corner would give zero hook lengths at removable cells.
fate: The original publication is \citet{framerobinsonthrall1954hook}, dated 1954 in the opened publisher record; the formula also appears in \citet[p.~1024]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}. The original full article was not accessible in this run.
present_status: As of November 2026: the formula is classical; the notebook date is one year late.

title: Multiplicity-free branching by removing a cell
notes: One sentence says that every irreducible of \(S_{n-1}\) occurs once, but the following line restricts to diagrams preceding \(\lambda\) in the Young graph.
statement: \(\operatorname{Res}^{S_n}_{S_{n-1}}V^\lambda\cong\bigoplus_{\mu\nearrow\lambda}V^\mu\), where \(\mu\nearrow\lambda\) means that \(\lambda/\mu\) consists of one removable cell. No other irreducible occurs.
reconstruction: The unrestricted wording is corrected using the immediately following notebook qualification.
fate: The classical branching theorem is proved in \citet[Theorems~2.9 and 5.8]{vershikokounkov2005approach}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the predecessor restriction is indispensable.

title: Paths, standard tableaux, and a Gelfand--Tsetlin basis
notes: Paths from the empty diagram to \(\lambda\) index basis vectors and count the degree of the representation.
statement: Successive multiplicity-free restrictions along \(S_1\subset\cdots\subset S_n\) decompose \(V^\lambda\) into one-dimensional joint eigenspaces for the centers of the subgroup algebras. Paths to \(\lambda\) index these lines, hence \(d_\lambda=f^\lambda\), the number of standard tableaux. Choosing a nonzero vector in each line gives a basis, unique only up to independent rescalings.
reconstruction: A canonical basis of lines does not choose phases or scales of vectors.
fate: See \citet[\S1 and Theorem~5.8]{vershikokounkov2005approach}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the classical branching-path interpretation is exact.

title: Counting paths between two fixed Young diagrams
notes: After calling combinatorial counting unsolved, the notes ask for the number of paths from a diagram of size \(n\) to a specified diagram of size \(m<n\).
statement:
For \(\mu\vdash m\), \(\lambda\vdash n\), \(\mu\subseteq\lambda\), the multiplicity of \(V^\mu\) in \(\operatorname{Res}^{S_n}_{S_m}V^\lambda\) is \(f^{\lambda/\mu}\). Equivalently, it counts standard tableaux of the skew shape. For \(r\geq\ell(\lambda)\), padding both partitions with zeros,
 \[
 f^{\lambda/\mu}=(n-m)!\det\left[\frac1{(\lambda_i-\mu_j-i+j)!}\right]_{i,j=1}^r,
 \]
 with \(1/k!=0\) for \(k<0\).
reconstruction: The determinant and the precise skew-tableau formulation are supplied here. The notebook does not specify a stronger demand such as a positive product formula or uniform asymptotics; such demands are not manufactured as open problems.
fate: Iterated branching gives the multiplicity interpretation. The classical Aitken determinant follows from Jacobi--Trudi, as explicitly derived in \citet[\S1, equations~(1.1)--(1.2)]{stanley2011skew}; the latter is a checked later exposition, not a claim that the formula originated in 2011.
present_status: As of November 2026: the literal finite counting problem has an exact determinant; no precise unsolved strengthening is recorded.

title: The assertion that total path counting is unsolved
notes: The notebook says \ru{Комбинаторная задача подсчета не решена} and mentions only Frobenius's formula, despite having just written the hook formula.
statement: For paths from the empty diagram, the hook formula already counts them. For two fixed endpoints, the skew determinant in the preceding item gives an exact count. Without an additional restriction on the permitted formula or asymptotic regime, the stated unsolved assertion is false.
reconstruction: The two possible literal readings are distinguished; neither supports an identified open problem.
fate: Compare \citet{framerobinsonthrall1954hook} and \citet[equation~(1.2)]{stanley2011skew}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the claim cannot be retained as evidence of an open counting problem.

title: First-row length detected by invariant vectors
notes: The first row is characterized by restriction to symmetric subgroups and the appearance of an invariant vector.
statement: For the standard inclusion \(S_m\subset S_n\), \((V^\lambda)^{S_m}\ne0\) if and only if \(m\leq\lambda_1\). Thus \(\lambda_1=\max\{m:(V^\lambda)^{S_m}\ne0\}\).
reconstruction: This follows by iterating the branching theorem: the one-row partition \((m)\) must be a subdiagram of \(\lambda\).
fate: This is an elementary consequence of the classical branching rule, verified in \citet[Theorem~5.8]{vershikokounkov2005approach}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the representation-theoretic characterization is exact.

title: Finite Plancherel measure
notes: The regular representation is described by functions on a symbol resembling \(S^n\); weights are \((\dim\lambda)^2/n!\).
statement: \(\mathbb C[S_n]\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n}V^\lambda\otimes(V^\lambda)^*\); therefore \(\sum_\lambda d_\lambda^2=n!\), and \(\mathrm{Pl}_n(\lambda)=d_\lambda^2/n!\) is a probability measure on partitions of \(n\).
reconstruction: The group is \(S_n\), not a sphere or a Cartesian power.
fate: See \citet[p.~1024]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}.
present_status: As of November 2026: this is the classical finite-group Plancherel measure.

title: The coherent Plancherel measure on infinite Young paths
notes: The notes pass to infinite paths and conditional probabilities for adding a cell.
statement:
Give a specified length-\(n\) path ending at \(\lambda\) mass \(d_\lambda/n!\). The resulting coherent probability measure has level marginal \(d_\lambda^2/n!\). Its growth transition is
 \[
 p(\lambda,\nu)=\frac{d_\nu}{(n+1)d_\lambda}\quad(\lambda\nearrow\nu,\ |\lambda|=n).
 \]
 The dimension identity for induction makes the transition probabilities sum to one.
reconstruction: These precise cylinder and transition probabilities expand the notebook shorthand.
fate: The infinite path measure is described in \citet[p.~1025, before Theorem~2]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}. The paper was received 14 December 1976 and presented 17 December 1976, then printed in 1977; those editorial dates do not establish an earlier public preprint.
present_status: As of November 2026: the coherent growth process is established.

title: Gelfand asks for an infinite-dimensional Plancherel formulation
notes: Gelfand asks for a continuous, infinite-dimensional analogue of Plancherel's formula.
statement: For finitary \(S_\infty\), a precise interpretation in the subsequent discussion is the spectral measure of the Young-path commutative subalgebra in the regular representation. The notebook does not specify a unique general Plancherel theorem for arbitrary infinite-dimensional groups.
reconstruction: A type-I direct integral over irreducible representations is not silently substituted for this question: the regular von Neumann algebra of \(S_\infty\) is a type \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor.
fate: The specific path-space realization and the type \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor are explicit in \citet[p.~1025]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}; this supplies only a partial match to the unqualified request.
present_status: As of November 2026: the specific construction is known; the broader requested object is not uniquely determined.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Plancherel limit shape in half-rotated coordinates
notes: The page displays uniform convergence in probability to \(\frac2\pi(X\arcsin X+\sqrt{1-X^2})\), but interchanges the sum and difference in the coordinate definition and omits the exterior formula.
statement:
For nonnegative row-column coordinates \(x,y\), set \(X=(x-y)/2\), \(Y=(x+y)/2\), and let \(\widetilde\lambda(X)\) be the upper boundary of the rotated diagram. Under \(\mathrm{Pl}_n\),
 \[
 \sup_X\left|n^{-1/2}\widetilde\lambda(\sqrt n X)-\Omega(X)\right|
 \longrightarrow0
 \quad\hbox{in probability},
 \]
 where \(\Omega(X)=\frac2\pi(X\arcsin X+\sqrt{1-X^2})\) for \(|X|\leq1\), and \(\Omega(X)=|X|\) otherwise.
reconstruction: The corrected coordinates and the exterior branch are checked against the 1977 paper. Their normalization has half the coordinates used in many later accounts.
fate: This is \citet[Theorem~1, pp.~1024--1025]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}, received December 1976 and published in 1977.
present_status: As of November 2026: the limit-shape theorem is established with these conventions.

title: Almost-sure convergence along coherent paths
notes: The notes separately assert convergence almost everywhere for infinite diagrams, interpreted as paths.
statement: For almost every infinite path under the coherent Plancherel measure, the uniformly rescaled boundary at level \(n\) converges uniformly to \(\Omega\). The assertion uses that coupling of the marginals, not an unspecified coupling of independent samples.
reconstruction: The ambient probability space is made explicit.
fate: This is \citet[Theorem~2, p.~1025]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}.
present_status: As of November 2026: almost-sure pathwise convergence is established.

title: Asymptotic first-row length
notes: The displayed corollary has \(\lambda_1/(2\sqrt n)\) near one and is called a solution of Ulam's problem.
statement:
For every \(\varepsilon>0\),
 \(\mathrm{Pl}_n\{|\lambda_1/(2\sqrt n)-1|<\varepsilon\}\to1\). The same first-order statement holds for the first column by transposition.
reconstruction: The missing terminal probability limit is supplied. Uniform boundary convergence alone does not control arbitrarily thin outer rows; the original proof also invokes a bound on expected first-row length.
fate: See \citet[Corollary~1 and its proof, p.~1026]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the first-order law is proved; it is not itself a fluctuation theorem.

title: The proposed white-noise central limit theorem
notes: The notes say \ru{Уклонения дают белый шум} and display fourth roots in both the argument and prefactor of an uncentered boundary functional; the test-function class and limiting distribution are unspecified.
statement:
A verified later formulation uses full rotated coordinates \(x=2X\), profile \(\bar\lambda_n(x)=2n^{-1/2}\widetilde\lambda(\sqrt n x/2)\), and \(\Omega_{\rm full}(x)=2\Omega(x/2)\). Put \(\Delta_n(x)=\frac{\sqrt n}{2}(\bar\lambda_n(x)-\Omega_{\rm full}(x))\). For any finite collection of polynomials \(p\), their integrals against \(\Delta_n\) converge jointly to those against the generalized Gaussian field
 \[
 \Delta(2\cos\theta)=\frac1\pi\sum_{k\geq2}\frac{\xi_k}{\sqrt k}\sin(k\theta),\qquad 0<\theta<\pi,
 \]
 with independent standard Gaussian \(\xi_k\). This field is not spatial white noise.
reconstruction: This is a later mathematically precise substitute, not a transcription repair or a claim that the 1977 speaker proved Kerov's theorem. The mode weights \(k^{-1/2}\), the vanishing area fluctuation, and polynomial-test topology are part of the correction.
fate: Kerov announced the central limit theorem in 1993. \citet[Introduction, Theorem~7.1, and \S9]{ivanovolshanski2002kerov} give a full account, published in the 2002 volume and posted to arXiv in 2003; their introduction distinguishes the 1993 announcement and 1999 unpublished notes.
present_status: As of November 2026: the later generalized-Gaussian theorem is proved; the notebook fourth-root formula is not a correct statement of it.

title: An unidentified stationarity assertion
notes: The words \ru{марковость и стационарность проверяются} immediately follow the fluctuation formula, without naming the process or action.
statement: Plancherel growth is Markov with the transition probabilities above, but the unrescaled shape process is not stationary: the number of cells is deterministically \(n\). A stationary process of rescaled fluctuations would require an additional time parametrization and an identified law, neither of which is given.
reconstruction: The known Markov construction does not identify what stationarity meant in this position on the page.
fate: The path construction is checked in \citet[p.~1025]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}; the fluctuation source \citet[\S7]{ivanovolshanski2002kerov} does not identify this notebook sentence.
present_status: As of November 2026: the Markov part has a precise interpretation, while the stationarity claim remains unidentified.

title: Row insertion connects permutations and Plancherel diagrams
notes: A bumping map into diagrams is credited to Knuth (1970) and a 1961 author written as Shenstead.
statement: Schensted insertion associates to a permutation of \(n\) a pair of standard tableaux of the same shape \(\lambda\). This correspondence is bijective, so a uniform permutation has insertion shape distributed by \(d_\lambda^2/n!\). Its longest increasing subsequence has length \(\lambda_1\).
reconstruction: The 1961 author is C. Schensted. Knuth's 1970 paper extends the correspondence; the distinction between a pair of tableaux and just a diagram is restored.
fate: See \citet[Theorems~1--3]{schensted1961longest} and \citet[\S\S2--3]{knuth1970permutations}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the classical insertion mechanism exactly transfers the Plancherel law to increasing subsequences.

title: Ulam's problem for a random real sequence
notes: For uniform \(x_i\in[0,1]\), the notes ask for the greatest increasing-subsequence length and state \(2\sqrt n\). The displayed maximum is over \(r\), but the subsequence indices end at \(n\).
statement: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent uniform random variables on \([0,1]\), and let \(L_n=\max\{r:\exists i_1<\cdots<i_r,\ X_{i_1}<\cdots<X_{i_r}\}\). Then \(L_n/(2\sqrt n)\to1\) in probability. The same holds for any independent identically distributed continuous law, since its ranks form a uniform permutation.
reconstruction: Independence, continuity, and the terminal index \(r\) are supplied. With continuous laws, strict and weak inequalities agree almost surely.
fate: The uniform version is \citet[Corollary~2, p.~1027]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}; the rank reduction uses \citet[Theorems~1 and 3]{schensted1961longest}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the first-order Ulam problem is solved.

title: The marked surface group
notes: The group \(FG_g\) has generators \(a_1,\ldots,a_g,b_1,\ldots,b_g\) and relation \(\prod_i[a_i,b_i]=1\).
statement: For a compact connected oriented surface \(\Sigma_g\), this is a presentation of \(\pi_1(\Sigma_g)\). A marked Riemann surface specifies an identification of its fundamental group with this fixed group; the orientation determines the integral intersection form on its abelianization.
reconstruction: Marking matters because the same abstract representations are compared while the complex structure varies.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, equation~(2.2.6) and Definition~2.2.6]{tyurin1978periods}. The survey was received 19 April 1977 and published in the 1978 volume; its introduction dates the underlying lectures to 1973.
present_status: As of November 2026: the group and marking are standard.

title: Dimension of the general linear character variety
notes: The notes subtract the relation and conjugacy dimensions to obtain \(2(g-1)n^2+2\), calling the quotient an algebraic variety with singularities.
statement:
For \(g\geq2\), the irreducible locus of
 \(\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_1(\Sigma_g),GL_n(\mathbb C))/\!/GL_n(\mathbb C)\)
 is smooth of complex dimension \(2(g-1)n^2+2\). A point of the affine quotient represents a semisimple conjugacy class; singular and reducible strata are not covered by the displayed tangent-dimension count.
reconstruction: At an irreducible representation, \(H^0(\Sigma_g,\operatorname{ad}\rho)\) and \(H^2\) each have dimension one. Euler characteristic gives \(\dim H^1=2+(2g-2)n^2\). This cohomological calculation checks the notebook's generic parameter count.
fate: The flat-bundle and representation interpretation is \citet[Ch.~II, \S2]{tyurin1978periods}; the explicit tangent-space argument is an editorial reconstruction of the familiar generic count.
present_status: As of November 2026: the generic dimension is correct; the unrestricted singular quotient needs the stated qualification.

title: The flat bundle associated to a representation
notes: The notes form \(E_\rho=U(X)\times V^n/\pi_1(X)\) and declare two representations analytically equivalent when their underlying bundles are isomorphic.
statement: For a representation \(\rho:\pi_1(X)\to GL_n(\mathbb C)\), quotient the trivial bundle on the universal cover by the compatible deck and linear action. Constant transition functions give a flat connection and a holomorphic bundle \(E_\rho\). Forgetting the flat connection sends the conjugacy class of \(\rho\) to the holomorphic isomorphism class of \(E_\rho\).
reconstruction: The deck-action convention must be used consistently; changing it changes \(\rho\) to the corresponding inverse convention, not the underlying correspondence.
fate: This is \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, equations~(2.2.3)--(2.2.5) and Definition~2.2.7]{tyurin1978periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the construction and equivalence relation are standard.

title: A packet is a fiber of forgetting the flat structure
notes: For fixed \(X,E\), a packet \(H(X,E)\) is a subset of the representation space.
statement: \(H(X,E)\) consists of conjugacy classes of representations whose associated holomorphic bundle is isomorphic to \(E\). Equivalently, it is the set of holomorphic connections on \(E\), modulo the action of \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\rm hol}(E)\). On a complex curve a holomorphic connection is flat because its holomorphic curvature is a two-form.
reconstruction: The quotient by bundle automorphisms is necessary before calling this a space of representation classes.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~II, Definition~2.2.8 and Exercises~1--5 to \S2, pp.~199, 204]{tyurin1978periods}. The survey explicitly refers the connection theory back to Atiyah's earlier work.
present_status: As of November 2026: the packet interpretation is established.

title: The packet dimension mixes GL(n) and fixed determinant
notes: An arrow labels \(H(X,E)\) as an affine space of dimension \((n^2-1)(g-1)\), although the ambient representations are in \(GL_n\).
statement: If \(E\) is a stable degree-zero rank-\(n\) bundle on a compact curve of genus \(g\geq2\), its holomorphic connections form an affine torsor for \(H^0(X,\operatorname{End}E\otimes K_X)\), of dimension \(n^2(g-1)+1\). Scalar automorphisms act trivially. If one also fixes the connection on \(\det E\), the modeling space is \(H^0(X,\operatorname{End}_0E\otimes K_X)\), of dimension \((n^2-1)(g-1)\).
reconstruction: The dimensions follow from Riemann--Roch and \(h^0(\operatorname{End}E)=1\). In rank one the GL(1) packet has dimension \(g\), whereas the notebook formula gives zero; this directly exposes the missing determinant constraint.
fate: The affine difference of connections and the dimension exercise are \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, Exercises~1 and 8, p.~204]{tyurin1978periods}. The corrected Riemann--Roch calculation is supplied here.
present_status: As of November 2026: the displayed formula is valid only for the fixed-determinant connection problem.

title: An ambiguous question about related bundles and representations
notes: A short line asks \ru{Расслоения связ. \(\Rightarrow\) что можно сказать о предст.?}; the word abbreviated as \ru{связ.} is uncertain.
statement: No specific relation between the two bundles is given. If holomorphic isomorphism is intended, the question asks about membership in a common packet; if deformation or another relation is intended, the notebook does not supply a precise condition or requested conclusion.
