reconstruction: The surrounding definition suggests packet equivalence, but that suggestion is not substituted for the uncertain word.
fate: The packet framework of \citet[Definitions~2.2.7--2.2.8]{tyurin1978periods} is relevant, but does not identify this isolated question's exact quantifiers.
present_status: As of November 2026: the local wording remains insufficient for a separate problem.

title: Any two irreducibles need not become analytically equivalent
notes: The manuscript states \ru{Любые два неприв. предст. эквивал. относит. нек-рой рим. пов.} and explains that they enter one packet.
statement: The literal assertion is false. Fix \(g\geq2\), \(0<\theta<2\pi\), and rank-one unitary characters \(\chi_0=1\), \(\chi_1(a_1)=e^{i\theta}\), with \(\chi_1=1\) on the remaining generators. Both are irreducible and satisfy the surface relation, but for every complex structure on \(\Sigma_g\) their underlying holomorphic line bundles are nonisomorphic.
reconstruction: Proof: an isomorphism would give a nowhere-zero holomorphic section of the unitary flat line bundle with character \(\chi_1\chi_0^{-1}\). In unitary parallel local frames, its log norm is harmonic; compactness makes it constant. Each local holomorphic coefficient then has constant modulus, hence is constant. The section is parallel, forcing the character to be trivial, a contradiction. An independent universal-cover derivation reaches the same conclusion. This is a correction of a false literal assertion, not a new open problem.
fate: \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, Exercise~10, p.~204]{tyurin1978periods} states that a packet cannot contain two distinct unitary representation classes. The 1973-lecture provenance establishes that the surrounding theory was not new in the 1978 printing; no claim is made that this exact notebook sentence is reproduced in the publication.
present_status: As of November 2026: the universal assertion is disproved by the checked rank-one example.

title: The affine fibration exists only over an appropriate bundle locus
notes: The notes draw \(R_C\to S_n(X)\), label it an affine bundle, and call \(S_n(X)\) the moduli of bundles.
statement: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex curve of genus \(g\geq2\). Over the moduli of stable degree-zero bundles, forgetting a holomorphic connection gives a torsor modeled on the cotangent bundle, with fiber dimension \(n^2(g-1)+1\); fixing determinant and its connection gives the trace-free version. The whole character variety does not map to stable-bundle moduli in this way: an irreducible flat bundle can have unstable underlying holomorphic bundle.
reconstruction: This is a restricted de Rham moduli statement. In a presentation using the Betti character variety, Riemann--Hilbert is analytic, so the notebook does not establish an algebraic affine bundle on the full Betti quotient.
fate: The difference-of-connections model is \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, Exercises~1--5]{tyurin1978periods}; the moduli-locus and torsor formulation make the suppressed hypotheses explicit.
present_status: As of November 2026: the restricted torsor picture is standard; the global unrestricted diagram is too strong.

title: Describe the packet of a fixed line bundle
notes: The typical problem is to describe \(H(X,L)\subset\mathbb C^{*\,2g}\) for a fixed one-dimensional holomorphic bundle.
statement:
For a compact connected Riemann surface \(X\), the packet is empty unless \(\deg L=0\). If \(\deg L=0\), choose one flat connection \(\nabla_0\); all others are \(\nabla_0+\eta\), \(\eta\in H^0(X,K_X)\). With a fixed sign convention for periods, the character set is a coset
 \[
 H(X,L)=\chi_0\left\{\gamma\longmapsto
       \exp\!\int_\gamma\eta:\eta\in H^0(X,K_X)\right\}.
 \]
reconstruction: Degree zero, the additive connection parameter, and the period convention are supplied. The next notebook calculations give an explicit divisor version of this description.
fate: The precise packet question is answered by \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, Exercises~1--5 and 12; \S3]{tyurin1978periods}; the logarithmic construction is also the introduction to \citet{tyurin1977periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the rank-one packet is explicitly described; there is no residual open inverse problem here.

title: Constant transition functions and degree zero
notes: The line bundle is represented by a cocycle in \(\mathcal O_X^*\), and comes from a character if a representative has constant transition functions.
statement: The forgetful map \(H^1(X,\mathbb C^*)\to H^1(X,\mathcal O_X^*)\) has image \(\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)\). Thus a holomorphic line bundle on a compact Riemann surface admits a flat structure exactly when its degree is zero; many flat structures can have the same holomorphic image.
reconstruction: This is a statement about existence of a constant cocycle representative, not that an arbitrarily chosen holomorphic transition cocycle is already constant.
fate: See \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, Definitions~2.2.1--2.2.2 and Exercise~5]{tyurin1978periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the line-bundle criterion is established.

title: A meromorphic section gives an integral-residue differential
notes: When transition functions are constant, the local \(df_i/f_i\) glue to one meromorphic differential. Its poles are simple and its residues are integers.
statement: For a nonzero meromorphic section of a flat line bundle, \(\omega=df_i/f_i\) is global. At a zero or pole of local order \(m\in\mathbb Z\), it has residue \(m\). Hence \(\sum_x\operatorname{Res}_x\omega=0\), and its residue divisor is the divisor of that section, of degree zero.
reconstruction: The residue sum and degree condition use compactness. The notation \([\omega]\) here records the residue divisor, not the full differential.
fate: This construction is explicitly given in \citet[Introduction, pp.~1359--1360]{tyurin1977periods} and \citet[Ch.~II, \S3]{tyurin1978periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the logarithmic differential construction is classical and exact.

title: Changing a section changes the residue divisor by a principal divisor
notes: The notes say that two representatives give equivalent divisors.
statement: Two nonzero meromorphic sections of the same holomorphic line bundle differ by a nonzero meromorphic function \(h\). Their divisors differ by \(\operatorname{div}(h)\); for the same flat connection the associated differentials differ by \(dh/h\). Exponentiated periods of \(dh/h\) equal one.
reconstruction: Holding the flat connection fixed is essential for the displayed differential comparison.
fate: This is the divisor and exponential-integral correspondence in \citet[Introduction]{tyurin1977periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the gauge and divisor equivalence is established.

title: Constructing every character in a packet from a divisor
notes: Fix a divisor, construct a differential with its principal parts, and solve \(df/f=\omega+\omega_0\) on the universal cover, with \(\omega_0\) holomorphic.
statement: Let \(D=\sum m_pp\) be a degree-zero divisor representing \(L\). There exists a meromorphic one-form with only simple poles of residues \(m_p\); all such forms differ by \(H^0(X,K_X)\). Their exponential integrals are meromorphic on \(U(X)\), because integer residues make the local exponent single-valued at each pole. Their deck multipliers give exactly \(H(X,L)\), in a compatible divisor/character convention.
reconstruction: The residue theorem's degree-zero condition is the missing existence hypothesis. Local meromorphic integrability of this first-order equation really does follow from the integer residues.
fate: See \citet[Introduction, pp.~1359--1360]{tyurin1977periods} and \citet[Ch.~II, \S3]{tyurin1978periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: this solves the stated rank-one packet problem.

title: The trivial packet is the exponential of holomorphic periods
notes: The zero fiber is described as exponentials of primitives of holomorphic differentials.
statement: The homomorphism \(H^0(X,K_X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_1(X),\mathbb C^*)\), \(\eta\mapsto(\gamma\mapsto e^{\int_\gamma\eta})\), has trivial kernel and image the packet of \(\mathcal O_X\). Indeed, a kernel element gives a single-valued nowhere-zero holomorphic function \(e^{\int\eta}\) on compact \(X\), hence a constant, so \(\eta=0\). Every other nonempty line packet is a coset.
reconstruction: The injectivity proof identifies the affine dimension \(g\) and provides a second check on the erroneous GL(1) dimension in P000702.
fate: Compare \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, Exercise~12(a), pp.~204--205]{tyurin1978periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the trivial packet and its translates are explicitly understood.

title: A marked character packet determines the curve through Torelli
notes: The notes claim that the surface can be recovered uniquely from a packet, by a theorem written as Terelli.
statement: Regard a nonempty packet as its embedded analytic subset in the character torus of the fixed oriented marked surface. Translating it to the identity gives the trivial packet; its tangent space identifies \(H^{1,0}(X)\subset H^1(\Sigma_g,\mathbb C)\). Together with the integral lattice and intersection pairing this gives the principally polarized Jacobian, which determines \(X\) up to isomorphism by Torelli.
reconstruction: The embedding, integral marking, and polarization are indispensable. An abstract affine space of dimension \(g\), or an unpolarized torus without the retained data, is not the claimed invariant.
fate: This is the content of \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, Exercises~12--13, pp.~204--205]{tyurin1978periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the Torelli conclusion is valid with the retained marking and polarization.

title: Unitary characters select a unique point of each line packet
notes: A small diagram marks unitary characters beside the Jacobian family; its circular central symbol is uncertain.
statement: The map \(\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_1(X),U(1))\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)\) is a bijection of real tori. Thus each degree-zero line packet contains exactly one unitary character. This is a real analytic selection, not a holomorphic section of the complex character torus.
reconstruction: The precise assertion reconstructs the diagram using rank-one unitary flat-bundle theory; the uncertain central glyph is not identified as a theta divisor.
fate: Uniqueness is \citet[Ch.~II, \S2, Exercise~10]{tyurin1978periods}; the adjacent Jacobian construction in Exercise~12 supplies the line-bundle setting.
present_status: As of November 2026: the unitary character parametrization is standard.

title: Schwarzian derivative and its chain rule
notes: The notes define \(S(f)=(f''/f')'-\frac12(f''/f')^2\) and give its composition rule, with zero Schwarzian for fractional-linear coordinate changes.
statement:
For a locally univalent holomorphic map,
 \[
 S_z(f)=\frac{f^{(3)}}{f'}-\frac32\left(\frac{f''}{f'}\right)^2,\qquad
 S_t(f\circ g)=(S_z(f)\circ g)(g')^2+S_t(g).
 \]
 A Möbius map has zero Schwarzian; postcomposition by one leaves \(S_z(f)\) unchanged.
reconstruction: Local univalence is needed away from the meromorphic singularities considered next.
fate: See \citet[\S1, properties~1--2]{tyurin1977periods} and \citet[Ch.~I, \S2]{tyurin1978periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the classical chain rule is exact.

title: Schwarzians require a projective atlas to become quadratic differentials
notes: After the chain rule, the notes say that general quadratic differentials result.
statement: Local Schwarzians transform as a projective connection under arbitrary holomorphic coordinate changes. After choosing a projective atlas, whose transition functions are Möbius, the extra Schwarzian term vanishes and the resulting expressions can be compared as quadratic differentials. The difference of two projective connections is intrinsically a quadratic differential.
reconstruction: Choosing the projective structure is essential; the notebook suppresses that choice.
fate: The projective-atlas assumption is explicit in \citet[Introduction and Definition~1.2]{tyurin1977periods}.

title: Double poles and the leading coefficient called a residue
notes: The margin allows poles of order at most two and calls the coefficient of \((dz/z)^2\) a residue.
statement:
If a meromorphic map has local degree \(m\geq1\), its Schwarzian is
 \[
 S_z(f)=\frac{1-m^2}{2z^2}+O(z^{-1}).
 \]
 For a quadratic differential with a double pole, the coefficient \(a\) of \(a(dz/z)^2\) is invariant under a local holomorphic change of parameter. This is not the residue of a one-form.
reconstruction: This is a necessary local property of a meromorphic Schwarzian, not a sufficient criterion for an arbitrary quadratic differential to have a meromorphic Schwarzian primitive. Resonant logarithmic terms require additional conditions.
fate: The terminology and necessary coefficient are in \citet[\S1, property~4 and equations~(1.3)--(1.4)]{tyurin1977periods}. The stronger sufficiency claim in its following property~5 is not used here; it does not match anything explicitly asserted in the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026: the leading coefficient statement is exact; no converse is inferred.

title: Schwarzian integration and projective monodromy
notes: The scan, in a diagram omitted from the plain transcription, reads \(f(g(u))=\rho(g)(f(u))\) and says that this reconstructs \(\rho\).
statement: On a Riemann surface with a fixed projective atlas, a holomorphic quadratic differential locally gives \(S(f)=q\), equivalently \(f=y_1/y_2\) for independent solutions of \(y''+\tfrac12q\,y=0\). Analytic continuation on the universal cover produces a locally univalent developing map and a conjugacy class \(\rho:\pi_1(X)\to PGL_2(\mathbb C)\) satisfying the displayed equivariance. For meromorphic data, continuation first gives monodromy of the punctured surface; it descends across poles only under the requisite local meromorphic integrability conditions.
reconstruction: The second-order equation and the distinction between the closed and punctured surface make the notebook's abbreviated reconstruction precise. The stronger uniqueness theorem of the 1977 paper is not imported as an occurrence absent from these pages.
fate: See \citet[\S1, Definitions~1.1--1.3 and equation~(1.6)]{tyurin1977periods} and \citet[Ch.~II, equation~(2.2.7)]{tyurin1978periods}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the projective monodromy construction is established with the indicated local hypotheses.
